title: Sequoyah’s syllabary created a written language for the Cherokee
summary: This article covers Sequoyah, a Cherokee silversmith who invented a written syllabary for the Cherokee language in the early 1800s, creating 86 characters representing syllable sounds that enabled the Cherokee to achieve near-universal literacy within years.
problem_solved: It solved the problem of the Cherokee people having no written language, enabling literacy, cultural preservation, and written communication.
why_valuable: This is historically significant as it demonstrates how one person's innovation can create written language for an entire culture in just 6 years, with adoption so rapid that skeptics thought it was magic.
